# MDN001 `double-precision`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

A `double precision` (or `double complex`) declaration.

## Why

`double precision` fixes the precision in the type name: changing the working precision means
editing every declaration. A named kind parameter (`real(rk)`, with `rk` from `iso_fortran_env` or
a project kind module) changes everywhere at once.

## Reported

```fortran
double precision :: x
```

## Preferred

```fortran
real(real64) :: x
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[MDN001] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = MDN001` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `MOD001` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
